construction.shape: A standing signed claim, minted by the writing credential at card creation, living in the content root beside the card it attributes
construction.record: Ed25519( writing credential ; LP("done/attrib/v1") || LP(dec v) || LP(workspace_id) || LP(card_id) || LP(actor_id) || LP(actor_kind) || LP(credential_id) || LP(dec epoch) || LP(hex content_commitment) )
construction.commitment: SHA-256( LP("done/attrib-body/v1") || LP(card_id) || LP(body at creation) )
construction.residence: In the content root, in a write-once map keyed by card id. §7.6 already requires attribution evidence to be portable workspace material that is checkpointed, stored and restored with the workspace rather than a separate operator archive — this is that, at the cheapest possible cost
construction.why_no_seq: The envelope position is deliberately not bound. Verifying it would tie every claim to row 5’s chain and therefore force chain retention, and a binding whose verification forces retention is not free in a row whose purpose is to reduce retention. Acceptance is already implied: a record only reaches the content root through an accepted envelope
construction.two_questions: The signature says a credential made this claim. The commitment says whether the card still holds what was claimed about. A card edited after creation verifies and is not exact, which is the honest reading of card-creation attribution rather than a defect in it
construction.storage_bound: One record per card, minted once, never updated. Attribution costs a constant multiple of what the cards already cost and retires on exactly the event §4.5 already says retires it — a card’s deletion under compaction
construction.retention_effect: §6.1’s trim collapses the store to one state record under the current generation and the records come with it, so verifying historical authorship stops requiring historical generations. §13.7’s two retention questions stop being different sizes

not_here.primitives: Ed25519 and SHA-256 KATs are row 1’s, in test/vectors/algorithm-suite.json.
not_here.checkpoint: How these records travel in a checkpoint is row 7.
not_here.retirement: What retires a claim is §4.5’s compaction, and the replica-acknowledgement protocol it waits on is §10.4’s.

laptop.role: The credential that made the claim. §7.4 lets it sign only its own operations, and a claim is one.

phone.role: Another admitted credential. It may not assemble a claim about the laptop’s write, and cannot.

vectors.name: human-created-card
vectors.why: The ordinary case: a person creates a card on their laptop at epoch 7.

vectors.name: system-actor-import
vectors.why: An imported card, attributed to the system actor (§9.2) and signed by the importing device’s credential. The system actor is not a member and holds no credential of its own (§4.8).

vectors.name: empty-card
vectors.why: A card created empty and typed into afterwards — the ordinary creation path in this product, and the case where the commitment is expected not to match later.

must_fail.name: assembled-by-another-credential
must_fail.mutate: The phone signs a claim about a card the laptop created. **This is §13.7’s named failure** — a newly assembled tuple beside somebody else’s work — and it fails because the record is signed over the tuple by the credential making the claim rather than copied from an envelope.

must_fail.name: lifted-to-another-card
must_fail.mutate: The laptop’s genuine claim, re-keyed under a different card id. Isolates `card_id`, which is what stops a record being moved to a card its actor never created.

must_fail.name: reattributed-actor
must_fail.mutate: Change the attributed actor while keeping the signing credential.

must_fail.name: reattributed-actor-kind
must_fail.mutate: Change `human` to `system`. A separate field because the kind changes what the UI says and what §4.8 permits, and a claim that moves between kinds is not the same claim.

must_fail.name: reattributed-credential
must_fail.mutate: Name a different credential inside a record the laptop signed, **verified under the key that actually signed it**. Holding the verifier fixed is what makes this test the binding: fetching the named credential’s key instead would fail on the key and prove nothing about the field.

must_fail.name: wrong-workspace
must_fail.mutate: Verify the claim against another workspace.

must_fail.name: wrong-epoch
must_fail.mutate: Move the claim to another epoch. The epoch is what a verifier resolves the credential-to-actor authorization against (§13.5), so a movable epoch would let a claim borrow a different roster.

must_fail.name: substituted-commitment
must_fail.mutate: Replace the body commitment with one for different text. The commitment makes the claim falsifiable; a substitutable one would make it merely decorative.

must_fail.name: wrong-version
must_fail.mutate: Claim record version 2 for a version-1 record.

must_fail.name: aad-only-renumbered-label
must_fail.mutate: Verify under "done/attrib/v2". The label is where this carrier authenticates its own version (row 1).
